us_watchlist.notes:
Nubank (NU) as a high-quality "category leader" within the fintech sector that is currently being undervalued by the market
. The investment thesis for Nubank is built on three main pillars: its growth profile, its valuation compared to historical norms, and its ability to leverage AI.
Growth and Market Position
Nubank is identified as a category leader with a "superior business model"
. Despite a broader market sell-off in fintech and internet stocks, Nubank continues to show strong fundamental performance, growing its business at a rate of +20% to +50% year-over-year
.
Valuation and Potential Re-rating
The analysis emphasizes a significant disconnect between Nubank's growth and its current market valuation:
Historical Context: Businesses with Nubank's model have historically commanded price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples of ~25x or higher
.
Current Discount: Nubank is currently trading at approximately 10 – 12x P/E on a 3-year forward basis
. The sources note that this type of valuation is typically reserved for "cyclical, slow-growing businesses," which does not reflect Nubank’s actual trajectory
.
Upside Opportunity: If Nubank can prove its earnings growth over the next few years, the author believes the stock could experience a 2 – 3x re-rating as it returns to more appropriate historical valuation levels
.
AI-Driven Competitive Advantage
Nubank is categorized as a "user of AI" rather than an infrastructure provider
. The analysis argues that forward-looking incumbents like Nubank will benefit most from AI by leveraging their "large proprietary datasets" to:
Know Customers Better: Use data to predict consumer behavior and determine when to re-engage them
.
Improve Economics: Specifically, Nubank can use AI to more accurately underwrite loans, which is a critical function for a digital bank
.
Enhance Product Stickiness: By embedding AI within their existing platforms, the author believes incumbents like Nubank will pull further away from slower-to-adopt competitors
.
Investment Monitoring
To manage the risks associated with fintech investments, the sources mention that AI-driven web-scraping tools and automated data pulls from government databases are used to triangulate loan quality across fintech holdings like Nubank
. This allow the investor to monitor the health of the underlying loan portfolio in real-time
.

AppLovin is another of the portfolio's larger positions
.
Market Leadership: It is described as the "best-in-class performance ad platform" in the mobile gaming sector
.
Market Share: AppLovin currently captures approximately 25-30% of user-acquisition spend in mobile gaming
.
Financial Efficiency: The author highlights its exceptional efficiency, noting that the company generates 70% Free Cash Flow margins
.

A newer addition to the portfolio, Unity is viewed as a "great business buried under years of self-inflicted wounds"
.
Operational Turnaround: The thesis relies on new CEO Matt Bromberg, who has a track record of rebuilding monetization stacks at Zynga
.
Unique Data Advantage: Unity's engine powers ~70% of mobile games, giving it "engine-level" visibility into user behavior (session length, in-app purchases) that competitors like AppLovin cannot see
.
The "Vector" Platform: Unity is ramping its new AI-driven ad targeting platform, Vector, toward a $1BN run-rate
. The author expects the stock to compound at 25% or better annually over the next 3-5 years
.

DoorDash is cited as a high-quality platform that has been "abandoned" as capital flows into semiconductors
.
Resilient Business Model: The author uses the example of ChatGPT's failed commerce initiative to argue that incumbent platforms like DoorDash have durable business models because consumer habits (saved payments, loyalty points) are sticky
.
Efficiency Gains: Like other portfolio holdings, DoorDash is expected to use AI to enhance existing products and pull away from slower competitors
.
Deep Discount: It is currently trading at a valuation typically reserved for slow-growing, cyclical businesses, providing what the author considers an attractive entry point for long-term investors
.

Sea Ltd is one of Hayden Capital’s larger positions
. The investment thesis centers on the belief that the company is undergoing a proactive reinvestment cycle rather than a defensive one
.
The Flywheel Effect: The author compares Sea’s current investments in Shopee VIP and its logistics network to Amazon’s launch of Prime and FBA in 2005-2006
. This creates a "flywheel" where free shipping drives order density, which lowers logistics costs, allowing for further reinvestment
.
Proven Results: Shopee VIP members already drive 20% of total GMV and order 3x more frequently than non-members
.
Valuation Gap: Despite generating $4.5BN in Free Cash Flow in 2025 and seeing GMV growth accelerate to +30% y/y, the stock trades at its lowest multiples since 2023
.

Mercado Libre is identified as the leading e-commerce platform in Latin America
.
Category Dominance: It is grouped among "category leaders" with superior business models that are growing between +20-50% year-over-year
.
AI Implementation: As a "user of AI," Mercado Libre is expected to leverage its large proprietary datasets to know customers better and improve conversion rates, making its business model more durable
.
Valuation Potential: Trading at roughly 10-12x P/E on a 3-year forward basis, the author believes the stock could see a 2-3x re-rating if it continues to prove its earnings growth
.

aif_investor_meets.notes:
# Prompt: Portfolio Intelligence Report — Single-File HTML Dashboard --- ## ROLE You are a senior equity research analyst AND a world-class frontend engineer. You will produce a fully self-contained, single-file HTML investment portfolio intelligence report that is production-ready, visually polished, and deployable directly to Netlify by dropping the file into the deploy zone. --- ## TASK Build a single `index.html` file that is a **tabbed portfolio intelligence dashboard** for [FUND NAME] based on the structured extraction below. The report must be: - Fully self-contained (no external JS dependencies except Google Fonts) - Deployable as a single file on Netlify with zero build step - Presentable to investors — editorial quality, not a dev tool - Interactive: tab navigation, company card expand/collapse, bucket filter, search --- ## DESIGN SYSTEM ### Typography - Headings: `'Playfair Display'` serif (import from Google Fonts, weights 400/500/700/900) - Body + UI: `'DM Sans'` sans-serif (weights 300/400/500/600) - Numbers/codes: `'DM Mono'` monospace (weights 400/500) ### Color Palette (CSS variables in `:root`) ```css --ink: #0d0d0d; /* primary text */ --ink2: #2a2a2a; /* secondary text */ --ink3: #5a5a5a; /* muted text */ --ink4: #999; /* hint text */ --paper: #faf8f4; /* page background */ --paper2: #f3f0e8; /* surface background */ --paper3: #e8e4d8; /* border-adjacent fills */ --accent: #b8460a; /* primary accent (burnt orange) */ --accent2: #d4520c; /* lighter accent */ --green: #1a5c3a; --green-bg: #e8f4ed; --amber: #8a5200; --amber-bg: #fef6e4; --red: #8a1a1a; --red-bg: #fef0f0; --blue: #1a3a6c; --blue-bg: #eef2fb; --border: #d8d4c8; --shadow: 0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.06), 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.04); --shadow-lg: 0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); ``` ### Layout Rules - Max content width: 1160px, centered, padding 0 32px - Cards: white bg, 1px solid `--border`, border-radius 12px - Badges/tags: font-family mono, font-size 9–10px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08–0.1em - Section headings: Playfair Display, 28px, font-weight 700, letter-spacing -0.02em - Conviction meter: thin 4px bar, gradient left=accent → right=green - Tables: `--ink` header background with white text; alternating row tints - No gradients on backgrounds. No box-shadows except on cards. --- ## PAGE STRUCTURE The report has a **sticky top navigation bar** with tabs. Clicking a tab hides all other sections and shows only that one. All sections start hidden on load except the first. ### Tabs (in order): 1. **Market Outlook** — macro data, earnings table, core thesis 2. **Portfolio** — all company cards (filterable + searchable) 3. **Exits** — exited positions with rationale 4. **Peer Map** — comparison table 5. **Names Index** — every proper noun mentioned 6. **Analyst Note** — synthesis paragraph Sub-navigation within Portfolio tab: - Sub-tabs: Cyclicals | Misunderstood | Tailwinds (jump to bucket within the Portfolio section) ### Portfolio filter buttons (inside the Portfolio tab): - All Holdings | Cyclicals | Misunderstood | Tailwinds - Clicking a filter shows only cards with matching `data-bucket` attribute and hides empty bucket sections ### Search bar (inside Portfolio tab): - Text input matching against `data-name` attribute and card inner text --- ## JAVASCRIPT RULES (CRITICAL — these bugs must be avoided) 1. **Never name a function `scrollTo`** — it shadows `window.scrollTo` and breaks silently. Use `showPage(id)` instead. 2. Tab switching must use `showPage(id)` which: (a) hides all sections in `PAGE_SECTIONS` array, (b) shows the target section, (c) updates active class on nav buttons by matching `onclick` attribute string. 3. Sub-bucket nav calls `showBucket(bucketId)` which calls `showPage('portfolio')` then smooth-scrolls to the bucket div after a 60ms delay. 4. Filter buttons must have `data-bucket="..."` attribute so the reset function can find the "All" button with `querySelector('.filter-btn[data-bucket="all"]')`. 5. `DOMContentLoaded` must hide all sections except `market` on initial load. 6. Card expand/collapse: `toggleCard(btn)` toggles `.expanded` class on `btn.closest('.company-card')`. The `.card-modules` div inside is `display: none` by default and `display: block` when `.expanded` is present. 7. Scroll-to-top button: fixed position, bottom-right, appears when `scrollY > 300`, triggers `window.scrollTo({top:0, behavior:'smooth'})`. --- ## HTML STRUCTURE TEMPLATES ### Masthead ```html
``` ### Company Card ```html
``` ### Bucket Section ```html
``` ### Exit Card ```html
``` ### Peer Comparison Table ```html
``` ### Names Index ```html
``` --- ## CONTENT TO POPULATE Paste the full structured extraction below. The extraction is organized as: ### GLOBAL CONTEXT - Market outlook data (index-wise PAT growth, earnings season results) - Fund performance stats - Portfolio bucket framework - Core macro thesis ### PER COMPANY (repeat for each holding): - **[A] Identification** — full name, aliases, holding status, bucket - **[B] Investment thesis** — every reason, every number - **[C] Anti-thesis / risks** — explicitly stated concerns - **[D] Valuation** — all multiples, price levels, targets - **[E] Transaction history** — bought/added/trimmed/sold with reasons - **[F] Comparisons** — every peer comparison made - **[G] Management** — named individuals and observations - **[H] Catalysts** — near and medium term - **[I] Passing mentions** — incidental references - **[J] Verbatim quotes** — 2–5 high-signal direct quotes ### EXITS - Why each position was sold, rotation rationale ### GLOBAL SECTIONS - **[K]** Macro & sector views - **[L]** Portfolio construction philosophy - **[M]** Master names list — every proper noun with context ### ANALYST SYNTHESIS - Conviction map, notable contradictions, key risks to monitor --- ## BUCKET CLASSIFICATION Assign each company to exactly one bucket based on the extraction: | Bucket | Description | Badge color | ~% of book | |--------|-------------|-------------|------------| | `cyclical` | Commodity-linked; lowest-cost producer play | amber | ~4% | | `misunderstood` | Business model not recognized by street; re-rating potential | accent (burnt orange) | ~20% | | `tailwind` | Clean story; well-understood; growing fast; re-rating + earnings combo | green | ~76% | --- ## CONVICTION LEVELS → BAR WIDTH Map qualitative conviction to bar fill width: - Very High → 90–95% - High → 78–85% - Medium-High → 70–76% - Medium → 58–65% --- ## REQUIRED SECTIONS CHECKLIST Before finalizing, verify the HTML contains: - [ ] Masthead with fund name, alpha stat, description - [ ] Summary bar with 8 quick stats - [ ] Sticky nav with all tab buttons using `showPage()` / `showBucket()` - [ ] Data strip ticker - [ ] Market Outlook section: metric cards grid (2x3), earnings table, thesis box - [ ] Portfolio section: filter bar with `data-bucket` attrs, search input, 3 bucket sections - [ ] Each company card: conviction meter, thesis, metrics (3 cols), risks/catalysts, expand toggle, modules, quote - [ ] Exits section: exit cards with red top border - [ ] Peer comparison table - [ ] Names index grid - [ ] Analyst note box (dark background) - [ ] Footer - [ ] Scroll-to-top fixed button - [ ] JS: `showPage()`, `showBucket()`, `filterCards()`, `searchCards()`, `toggleCard()`, `DOMContentLoaded` init - [ ] NO function named `scrollTo` anywhere in the file --- ## OUTPUT FORMAT Output a single complete `index.html` file. No explanatory text before or after — just the raw HTML from `` to ``. The file must be ready to rename and drop into Netlify. --- ## EXTRACTION TO USE [PASTE YOUR FULL EXTRACTION HERE — the markdown document generated from the investor meet transcript, including all company modules A–J, global sections K–M, exits, and analyst synthesis]

"I have a prompt library HTML file that I want to update with new prompts. Please:
1. Read my existing HTML file (I will attach it)
2. Add the following new prompts to it — each as a new card in the appropriate section:
[paste your new prompts here, one by one, with this info for each:]

Prompt title:
Category: (forensic / valuation / concall / research / sector / mgmt / macro)
Tool: (Claude / ChatGPT / Perplexity / Gemini / NotebookLM)
Day: (Day 1 / Day 2 / Bonus)
Description: (1-2 lines on what it does)
The prompt text itself:

3. If a prompt fits a new category that doesn't exist yet, create a new section for it following the same card style as the existing sections.
4. Output the complete updated HTML file — do not summarise or truncate it.
Return the full file ready to deploy to Netlify."**

A few tips for using it well:
Upload the HTML file every time — don't just reference it by name. Attaching the actual file ensures Claude reads the exact current version and doesn't accidentally drop any existing prompts.
If you're adding many prompts at once, group them by category in your message — it helps Claude place them correctly without asking clarifying questions.
And if you want the new prompts tagged "Day 3" or "Bonus" or any custom label, just say so in the message — the badge colour and label will be added automatically.
